brief: One fixed neutral bust and sphere; vary lighting to teach 12 concepts.
notes: Requested square 1024-pixel illustrations; actual provider output dimensions are recorded separately.
Prompts and reference relationships are explicit. These are generated interpretations, not calibrated lighting simulations.

jobs.title: Key light
jobs.prompt:
Create ONE polished educational lighting-study image for a film vocabulary wiki, not a collage. Square 1024x1024 composition. This first study demonstrates KEY LIGHT and establishes a reusable subject for eleven later controlled relighting studies.

Subject and scene: a single smooth matte light-gray plaster head-and-shoulders sculpture of an adult androgynous person, hairless with simplified but realistic nose, eyelids, lips and ears. A quiet, neutral expression. A clearly inanimate sculpture, no skin texture, no clothing or jewelry. Its head faces straight toward camera, neither tilted nor turned. Entire head, both shoulders and the top of a plain cylindrical pedestal are visible. A small matte gray sphere rests on the same flat tabletop, to the viewer's right of the pedestal, with clear space between them. Neutral mid-gray seamless studio wall and tabletop. Exact frontal eye-level camera, centered balanced composition, medium-close framing, ordinary perspective, crisp detail across bust and sphere. The sculpture occupies about 65 percent of image height. No props other than pedestal and sphere.

Lighting lesson: one dominant neutral-white key light from viewer-left, about 45 degrees to the camera and 25 degrees above the face, medium apparent source size. It clearly models nose, cheek and neck. The viewer-left side is lit; the viewer-right side is in readable shadow. Very faint environmental fill only, no rim light, no backlight, no decorative color. Visible coherent cast shadows on the tabletop go away from the key. The background stays mid-gray. Neutral color balance. Preserve realistic shadow behavior. This should feel like a clean cinematography textbook render, attractive and materially convincing, not dramatic fantasy art.

No written words, numbers, labels, diagrams, arrows, visible fixtures, borders, watermark, or split panels. Show the actual result of the lighting, leaving titles to the webpage.

jobs.title: Fill light
jobs.prompt:
Relight the supplied image to create ONE educational film-lighting illustration, not a collage. Preserve EXACTLY the same sculpture identity and geometry, pose, pedestal, sphere position, tabletop, camera, framing, material, and square aspect ratio. The neutral matte light-gray plaster bust remains straight-on and inanimate. Change only lighting, shadow patterns, and the background illumination expressly requested below. Keep a neutral-white light color balance, with no stylized colored gels. Preserve the physical plausibility of nose shadows, under-chin shadows, sphere shadows, and cast shadows. No words, numbers, labels, arrows, light-fixture diagrams, additional props, split panels, borders, or watermark. Aim for a polished but restrained textbook studio rendering. The webpage will provide labels. 
Lighting lesson: Retain the original viewer-left key direction, its lit cheek and highlights. Add a broad low-intensity neutral fill from near the camera on viewer-right to raise the shadows on the right eye, cheek and neck. The lit side must not become substantially brighter. Make the shadow side clearly more readable and the facial contrast noticeably lower than in the reference, without erasing the key's direction. No added rim or background light. Keep the tabletop shadows softer and visible, not multiple hard crossed shadows.
